correctness.rationale: The ordered two-point convolution of {(u,v,uv)} has r(w)=q-1+q*1_{w=0} points after translating by (S1/2,S2/2), giving Cq=1+q^-1-q^-2. Expanding f=1+th and summing over S with exact q^-5 normalization yields a real quadratic form. The finite-field Fourier transform of the kernel K_k(w)=sum_{xy=w}psi(k1x+k2y) is 0 at t=0 and modulus q at nonzero dual t, so the real/imaginary axis-vs-mixed coefficients are as printed. Independently computed the Taylor coefficient from all ordered pairs and the Fourier spectrum for nontrivial random complex h over F3 and F5; deviations below 1.2e-15. With q odd, all four positive eigenvalues and exact multiplicities follow; scalar directions are a two-real-dimensional kernel. The local bound uses the quartic remainder in a fixed finite-dimensional norm and correctly disclaims q-uniform radii.
residual_risks: The positive coefficients are t^2 Taylor coefficients; usual Hessian eigenvalues are twice these numbers.
Uniformity only over perturbations at a fixed q, not an infinite-field uniform stability theorem.
